chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام
about a man who fled with his wealth from zakat, then bought land or a house with it. Is anything due on it?

So he said: No. Even if he made it into jewelry or silver pieces, nothing is due upon it. And whatever extra bounty he withheld from himself is greater than what he withheld from the right of Allah that would have been in it.

key_terms.أَرْضًا: land or real property purchased with the wealth
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms-tax due on qualifying wealth
key_terms.حَقِّ اللَّهِ: the right of Allah, meaning the divinely mandated due in the wealth
key_terms.حُلِيًّا: jewelry or ornaments made from the wealth
key_terms.فَرَّ: escaped or fled, here meaning he sought to avoid liability
key_terms.فَضْلِهِ: its surplus or extra bounty, referring to the greater benefit he deprived himself of

ai.seo_question: If someone avoids zakat by turning wealth into property or jewelry, is zakat still due on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that when wealth subject to zakat is converted into land, a house, jewelry, or silver pieces, zakat is no longer due on that transformed property in the described sense. At the same time, it carries an ethical warning that the person, by evading Allah’s right, has deprived himself of a greater divine blessing.
